item.title: Floating breakfast experience
item.description: A FLOATING breakfast experience popularised by resorts in Bali, and the Maldives has been introduced at Tambua Sands Beach Resort on Fiji’s Coral Coast. In a media statement, the adults-only resort said the breakfast experience allowed guests to have breakfast in their private plunge pools.
item.content:encoded:
A FLOATING breakfast experience popularised by resorts in Bali, and the Maldives has been introduced at Tambua Sands Beach Resort on Fiji’s Coral Coast.

In a media statement, the adults-only resort said the breakfast experience allowed guests to have breakfast in their private plunge pools.

“The meal is served on a floating tray and includes tropical fruit, pastries, juice, coffee, and other island-inspired selections,” the resort stated.

“The experience costs $89 per person. Guests can also request additional food and beverages, dietary accommodations, romantic touches, and arrangements for special occasions at an additional cost.”

Resort manager Angela Bob said the experience was designed to give guests a way to enjoy their surroundings while creating a memorable holiday experience.

“Our guests travel from around the world to experience the beauty of Fiji,” Ms Bob said.

“We wanted to create something unique that allows them to slow down, relax and truly enjoy their surroundings.

“The floating breakfast is more than a meal; it is an experience and a memory.”

Tambua Sands Beach Resort is located on Fiji’s Coral Coast and offers private villas, beachfront accommodation, and plunge pools.

The resort caters to adults and is set among tropical gardens overlooking the beach.

The floating breakfast is available to guests celebrating occasions such as honeymoons, anniversaries, and birthdays, as well as those looking to add a special experience to their stay.

item.title: DPM: Fiji imports too much
item.description: FIJI imports too much of what it consumes, said Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Commerce, Business Development and Public Enterprise Manoa Kamikamica. He made the comments during the commissioning of a new Food Processors Fiji facility at Batiri, Macuata earlier this week.
item.content:encoded:
FIJI imports too much of what it consumes, said Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Commerce, Business Development and Public Enterprise Manoa Kamikamica.

He made the comments during the commissioning of a new Food Processors Fiji facility at Batiri, Macuata earlier this week.

“We import too much of what we consume, and we remain exposed to global shocks in global supply chains, shipping costs and climate change disruption,” Mr Kamikamica said.

He said facilities such as the Batiri operation were important because they allowed locally produced agricultural commodities to be processed and converted into higher-value products within the country.

“Every facility, such as this one, takes local produce and adds value to it here, strengthens our resilience as a result and keeps the economic benefit within our communities.”

The Batiri facility is the first Food Processors Fiji operation on Vanua Levu and will source selected produce from farmers in surrounding communities.

The produce will be processed locally before finished products are supplied to existing and new markets.

He said the investment would strengthen Fiji’s agricultural supply chain while providing farmers with a local commercial market for their produce.

The commissioning follows the signing of a memorandum of understanding between the Ministry of Agriculture, Food Processors Fiji Limited, and the Batiri community.

Under the agreement, farmers will provide land and labour, while the company will provide investment and market access. The Government will support the sector through extension services, infrastructure, and policy.

Food Processors Fiji acting chief executive officer Vinal Chand said the commissioning marked a new chapter for the company’s operations in Batiri.

Mr Chand said the facility would focus on operating efficiently and sustainably while supporting increased production and access to markets.

item.title: Cooperatives to revitalise rural economies
item.description: FIJI is placing small businesses, micro-enterprises, and cooperatives at the heart of its strategy to revitalise rural economies and curb urban migration. Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Industries, Commerce, Business Development and Public Enterprises Manoa Kamikamica made the comment in his opening address at the Strengthening Pacific Cooperatives through Education, Training and Regional
item.content:encoded:
FIJI is placing small businesses, micro-enterprises, and cooperatives at the heart of its strategy to revitalise rural economies and curb urban migration.

Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Industries, Commerce, Business Development and Public Enterprises Manoa Kamikamica made the comment in his opening address at the Strengthening Pacific Cooperatives through Education, Training and Regional Cooperation workshop held at the Tanoa International Hotel in Nadi On Wednesday.

Mr Kamikamica outlined the Government’s plan to make staying in villages economically viable and attractive for future generations.

He said that a lack of rural income drove the migration toward urban centres. By strengthening the cooperative model, he said the Government aimed to flip this dynamic, allowing citizens to earn sustainable incomes directly within their communities. Mr Kamikamica said that boosting agricultural and village-based enterprises would create financial stability comparable to high-paying urban positions, retaining talent and supporting local growth across the islands.

The strategy focuses heavily on key agricultural sectors while expanding social and financial inclusion, he said.

Mr Kamikamica said the Government supported the establishment of 20 cooperatives for a group of 7000 farmers known as the New Valley Farmers, who were already expanding their reach by exporting produce like cowpea to New Zealand and root crops to Nauru.

He added the initiative highlighted youth and women’s empowerment, demonstrated by a Nausori women’s cooperative that received a Government-funded three tonne truck to transport market vendors and generate secondary hire revenue.

“With the combination of the cooperatives and the mining markets, we are trying to slowly flip the direction and make it more attractive, or as some people say, sexy, to stay back in the village and earn a proper living,”Mr Kamikamica said. “My hope is that in time, you can be in the village and earn 20, 30, 40,000. That will be good enough,that’s like someone earning 200,000 in town and those are some of the dreams that we are currently looking at in terms of cooperatives for Fiji.”

item.title: Record breaking month
item.description: FIJI recorded a total of 105,791 visitors who arrived in the country in July alone this year, marking the highest monthly visitor arrivals ever recorded. This is also the first time that monthly arrivals have exceeded the 100,000 mark.
item.content:encoded:
FIJI recorded a total of 105,791 visitors who arrived in the country in July alone this year, marking the highest monthly visitor arrivals ever recorded.

This is also the first time that monthly arrivals have exceeded the 100,000 mark.

The July figures represent an increase of 6.5 per cent compared to July 2025 when 99,311 visitors were recorded – an increase of 7.4 per cent compared to June 2026, which recorded 98,522 visitor arrivals.

According to the Fiji Bureau of Statistics (FBoS), visitor arrivals for July stood at 98,332 in 2024 and 93,483 in 2023.

FBoS acting chief executive officer Apisalome Tamani said of the 105,791 visitors, a total of 104,377 came by air while 1414 came by sea.

He said the sea arrivals were mostly seamen on fishing vessels (914) and 500 arrivals by yacht.

“For July 2026, visitors arriving for holiday purposes accounted for 80.1 per cent of total arrivals, 8.7 per cent came to visit their friends or relatives, 1.6 per cent came for business purposes, while 9.6 per cent visited Fiji for other reasons,” Mr Tamani said in the Bureau’s report released on Monday.

According to the Bureau’s statistics, the major source markets of Australia, New Zealand, USA, China, Continental Europe, Canada and the UK continued to dominate visitor arrivals in Fiji in July this year, accounting for 91.8 per cent of total arrivals.

Visitors from Australia totalled 45,907 (43.4 per cent); 28,430 visitors (26.9 per cent) from New Zealand; 13,428 (12.7 per cent) – USA; China – 3117 (2.9 per cent); Continental Europe – 3093 (2.9 per cent); Canada – 1722 (1.6 per cent); and UK – 1393 – 1.3 per cent.

Mr Tamani said majority of visitors were in the age range of 25-64 years (59.3 per cent), which accounted for the vast majority of the working age population.

Children aged 14 and below accounted for 18.3 per cent of the July visitor arrivals; 11.6 per cent were youths aged 15-24, with the remaining 10.8 per cent comprising those in the predominantly retirement age group of 65 and over.

Meanwhile, Mr Tamani said 15,694 Fiji residents departed the country during July – of which 13,665 (87.1 per cent) were for a short-term absence of under three months and 914 (5.8 per cent) were for an absence of three months to less than 12 months.

He added 1115 (7.1 per cent) of resident departures were for a longer-term absence of one yer or more.

item.title: Death probe review
item.description: THE investigation into the death of Police Constable Peniasi Racagi remains under review by the Office of the Director of Public Prosecutions (ODPP). The ODPP confirmed this in response to questions from this newspaper about the status of the investigation and whether forensic analysis of samples sent to New Zealand had been completed.
item.content:encoded:
THE investigation into the death of Police Constable Peniasi Racagi remains under review by the Office of the Director of Public Prosecutions (ODPP).

The ODPP confirmed this in response to questions from this newspaper about the status of the investigation and whether forensic analysis of samples sent to New Zealand had been completed.

“The matter is currently under review according to the ODPP standard procedures,” the ODPP confirmed.

Assistant Commissioner of Police Crime, Loraini Seru, confirmed the analysis report had been returned and submitted to the ODPP.

The Fiji Times also contacted New Zealand Police seeking clarification on when the samples were received, when testing was completed and other matters relating to the forensic analysis, and were directed back to Fiji Police.

“You will need to contact Fiji Police in the first instance here as this is their investigation.”

The samples were sent to New Zealand because of limitations with forensic equipment available locally.

Constable Racagi, who was based at the Lami Police Station, went missing during his night shift on February 20. His body was found floating near the beach behind the Lami Oceania Wesley Church the following morning.

item.title: 4 children in road accidents
item.description: FOUR children have been involved in separate road accidents across Fiji in just two days, leaving an eight-year-old dead and two others in hospital as the country heads into the school holidays. According to police, the eight-year-old boy was attempting to cross the road when he was struck by a vehicle driven by a 32-year-old man on the Queens Rd at Vakabalea, Navua on Tuesday evening.
item.content:encoded:
FOUR children have been involved in separate road accidents across Fiji in just two days, leaving an eight-year-old dead and two others in hospital as the country heads into the school holidays.

According to police, the eight-year-old boy was attempting to cross the road when he was struck by a vehicle driven by a 32-year-old man on the Queens Rd at Vakabalea, Navua on Tuesday evening.

Police said the man was expected to be questioned as investigations continue.

In another incident, police also reported two children aged eight and nine were struck by a vehicle along Adi Davila Rd in Nakasi on Wednesday.

The children allegedly crossed in front of a parked bus when they were hit by a vehicle. Both remain admitted at the Colonial War Memorial Hospital in Suva.

In a separate incident on Narewa Rd in Nadi, a nine-year-old girl was crossing the road when she was struck by a vehicle driven by a 52-year-old.

Police confirmed she is in stable condition at the Lautoka Aspen Hospital.

Assistant Commissioner of Police Operations Kasiano Vusonilawe has urged motorists and families to take greater care, particularly with school holidays and large gatherings expected across the country.

item.title: ‘Line-up’ disappoints Pickering
item.description: The absence of Indo Fijian contestants was one of the talking points as Suva prepared for the 1989 Hibiscus Festival, with committee chairman George Pickering expressing disappointment that none was sponsored to compete for the coveted Hibiscus Queen crown. The Fiji Times reported on August 15 of 1989 that 15 young women were contesting the coveted Hibiscus Queen crown.
item.content:encoded:
The absence of Indo Fijian contestants was one of the talking points as Suva prepared for the 1989 Hibiscus Festival, with committee chairman George Pickering expressing disappointment that none was sponsored to compete for the coveted Hibiscus Queen crown.

The Fiji Times reported on August 15 of 1989 that 15 young women were contesting the coveted Hibiscus Queen crown.

“I am personally disappointed that no Indian girls are taking part in the contest,” Mr Pickering said.

“Suva is a multi-racial city, and it was a pity that no Indian girls had been sponsored.”

Despite this, preparations for the carnival were progressing according to schedule and the organising committee was pleased with the response from business houses, despite having five fewer contestants than the previous year.

The frames for about 60 stalls had been erected along Cakobau Rd, with almost all the stalls already rented.

Cakobau Rd had been closed to traffic for the duration of the carnival to allow organisers and stall holders to complete preparations and ensure the area was ready for the crowds.

Financially, Mr Pickering was also confident the committee would raise a “significant amount”, despite the substantial sum collected during Hospital Week just two weeks earlier.

The committee had set a target of $50,000, while the previous year’s carnival had raised about $100,000.

The 1989 festival also promised attractive prizes for the winners. Miss Hibiscus 1989 was to receive a return trip for two to Vancouver, Canada while Miss Charity was to win a return trip for two to Honolulu.

Both prizes were courtesy of Canadian Airlines International as part of the airline’s 40th anniversary celebrations.

Adding to the occasion, the Fijian Hotel was to host all the contestants for a night following the carnival.

Tickets for the various festival programs were scheduled to go on sale from August 15, with a sales booth operating in front of the Central Morris Hedstroms from 10am to 4pm daily.

As Suva counted down to the carnival, the city was preparing once again for a week of colour, entertainment, competition and community celebration.

item.title: Civil servants warned against political activity ahead of General Election
item.description: Civil servants have been reminded to maintain strict political neutrality and impartiality ahead of Fiji’s forthcoming General Election. The reminder comes in Circular 14/2026 issued by Permanent Secretary for Civil Service Pita Tagicakirewa on August 3, reiterating the obligations of civil servants under the Civil Service Act 1999 and the General Orders.
item.content:encoded:
Civil servants have been reminded to maintain strict political neutrality and impartiality ahead of Fiji’s forthcoming General Election.

The reminder comes in Circular 14/2026 issued by Permanent Secretary for Civil Service Pita Tagicakirewa on August 3, reiterating the obligations of civil servants under the Civil Service Act 1999 and the General Orders.

The circular follows an earlier Circular 16/2025 on political activities by civil servants.

It states that civil servants must ensure their conduct, both in the workplace and in public, does not compromise or appear to compromise the political neutrality, integrity or reputation of the Civil Service.

“Civil servants must not engage in, make or publish any political activity or statement that is prohibited under the relevant provisions of the General Orders,” the circular states.

Civil servants have also been warned against using their official position, authority, government premises, working hours, government resources or access to official information for political purposes or in support of any political party or candidate.

The Permanent Secretary has directed all Permanent Secretaries and Heads of Departments to ensure the circular is brought to the attention of all officers under their responsibility.

They have also been instructed to adequately brief officers on their obligations regarding political neutrality and political activities and take appropriate measures to prevent government premises, resources and working hours from being used for prohibited political activities.

Any alleged breach must be promptly addressed in accordance with the Discipline Guideline and other applicable procedures.

The circular cites Section 6(12) of the Civil Service Act 1999, which requires civil servants to conduct themselves in a manner that upholds the values of the Civil Service.

The directive comes as political parties prepare for the next General Election, with the Government reinforcing the requirement that public servants remain politically neutral while carrying out their official duties.
